findings.title: A crafted opencode message crashes the app: the output + reasoning addition does not saturate
findings.source: The JSON `data` column of the `message` table in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db: $.tokens.output and $.tokens.reasoning (OpencodeScanner.swift:141-142)
findings.sink: Swift's checked `+` on two Int values, each clamped only from below (OpencodeScanner.swift:197)
findings.description: The scanner reads two per-group sums from SQLite: sum($.tokens.output) and sum($.tokens.reasoning). Each is clamped with max(0, x), which puts no upper bound on either value, and then the two are added with Swift's `+`, which traps on overflow. Only this addition skips CostAggregator.saturatingAdd. The CodexSessionScanner and ClaudeSessionScanner paths use it or clamp their subtractions.
findings.exploit_scenario: Write one assistant row into opencode.db with providerID set to a tracked alias (such as openai), a recent time_created, and tokens.output = 9223372036854775807 plus tokens.reasoning = 1. A REAL such as 1e300 also works, because sqlite3_column_int64 clamps it to Int64.max. SQLite's sum() does not overflow on a single row. On the next refresh the Swift addition hits SIGTRAP and the menu-bar app exits. The row stays in the database, so every relaunch and refresh crashes again until the row is removed.
preconditions: Write access to ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (another tool or a prompt-injected agent running as the same user)
opencode cost scanning is enabled for at least one vendor
findings.impact: Persistent denial of service: the app crashes on every refresh cycle, so all usage monitoring stops.
findings.fix: Use CostAggregator.saturatingAdd(max(0, output), max(0, reasoning)). Better still, clamp each column to a sane per-group ceiling before any arithmetic.
findings.evidence: L187 `let reasoning = Int(sqlite3_column_int64(stmt, 5))`; L197 uses a bare `+`. By contrast CostAggregator.add (CostAggregator.swift:16-30) and ClaudeSessionScanner L232 use saturatingAdd.
